subject: ESEM-MIMIC: Regression coefficients changed after reordering indicators

messages.author: a8a812eced9ab1d7
messages.subject: ESEM-MIMIC: Regression coefficients changed after reordering indicators
parts:
Hi,

I fitted an ESEM-MIMIC model (n = 1450; 74 ordinal indicators; 10 latent variables; one EFA block; six demographic predictors; DWLS estimation) and got good fit measures (CFI = .978; TLI = .976; RMSEA = .032; SRMR = .015). I, then, reordered the indicators (and the latent variables labels accordingly) in the model specification to better represent my underlying constructs and fitted the model again. As expected, the results for the measurement model were exactly the same (same fit inidces, same indicator distribution within the latent variables, equivalent factor loadings, and same factor covariances). However, the regression coefficients of the latent variables with the demographic predictors described an erratic pattern. Although each latent variable comprises the correct set of indicators, six latent variables have regression coefficients equal to those associated with the latent variable that occupied their position in the first (unordered) model, and two latent variables have regression coefficients completely different to those in the previous model. The remaining two latent variables got the same coefficients they had in the first model.

I would greatly appreciate your guidance on what might be going on. Below please find the lavaan's output for the regression results:
